Phone at 8 am. haha you will be lucky to get through.    I can understand the system to phone first thing in the morning for an appointment on that day if there is one available.
But the curious one is; I am told that we all must  phone on Monday 's for all appointments during the week.  So, if  on Wednesday I need to see a Doctor it's a no go situation;  either phone each morning at 8 and seldom get any joy. (even if you get through there's no appointments available for about 4 - 6 weeks) or wait until the following Monday and hope you get through before all the bookings are taken.  You can't win and it makes no sense.
After spending 11 hours at A & E Saturday night, no sleep at all, monitors all night long etc., discharged and instructed to see my doctor for heart medications etc. So  Monday,  today; I start phone at 8 a.m. at  9.30 I walk to the surgery (walking is very difficult for me).  I ask if report from hospital is through and if so I need an appointment to discuss medication and prescription  that I apparently need.   Ha, ha, ha, its funny if it wast so flipping stressful.   I am told, no appointments available.  Try tomorrow at 8 a.m. and so the circus will continues.  She says she can see the report from the hospital has been received but there is nothing she can do.  I tell her any doctor I don't care who.   Once again I am told to ring at 8 tomorrow.   So I shall get on the phone tomorrow at 8 a.m.  and continue with this circus.    Dealing with this sort of situation and guidelines laid down by who knows who is just so stressful.  I am not blaming the staff, they do what they can within the limits of an uncaring  system obviously founded by someone who has no idea of the needs of patients -  At 84 I have never ever encountered such a stressful interaction with a doctors surgery.     I never use a doctor unless really necessary but  been there done that  many times with this surgery.   My stories are  boring but really bad outcomes each time and I have given up and doctored myself or resorted to private consultations at The Ridgeway.   This time I can't  because it involves my heart.   By the way, twice I have managed to get an appointment and not been checked in. Waited patiently for an hour before going back to reception to find out what's happened!     Was told "oh dear........
As for the 10 minute rule it is hideous when you see a doctor that you have never met before, so we  end up with 3 minutes talk and 7 minutes of typing.
